subject: Ramp & burst pricing — MAP milestones and rate-card clarifications
messages:
From: Sedra Reyes <sreyes@greenwavehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: GreenWave Procurement <procure@greenwavehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up on MAP + ramp pricing questions

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and observability looked very promising. Before we take the MAP to our finance/procurement team, a few questions came up about how commercial milestones will interact with ramp pricing, burst/overage, and any caps while we evaluate: 

- What exactly counts as the "ramp" period in the MAP (months 1–3 vs. first N tokens)?
- How do overage/burst charges work if we exceed the committed volume during the ramp? Any hard caps or throttles?
- Are there discount milestones tied to the MAP milestones (e.g., once we hit a throughput/commit target)?
- Can you provide a clear, line-item rate card and an example invoice for a ramp scenario?

Procurement wants a short written summary we can include in the purchase approval packet. Can you send a single doc that ties MAP milestones to pricing and expected protections while we test?

Thanks — Sedra
Sedra Reyes
Director, Product Integrations
GreenWave Health
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sedra Reyes <sreyes@greenwavehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-02T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on MAP + ramp pricing questions

Hi Sedra —

Appreciate the clear list. I attached a focused MAP doc (Redwood_MAP_v2.pdf) and our current quarter rate card (RateCard_Q1_2026.xlsx). High level answers up front, then a proposed one-page summary you can drop into procurement: 

- Ramp definition: we recommend treating "ramp" as the first 90 days from go-live and/or the first 3M tokens (whichever is later). This gives time for traffic shaping and prompt optimization.

- Overage/burst: during the ramp we offer a two-tier protection: 
  * Soft-burst: up to +25% above the committed daily average allowed without immediate overage invoicing; usage is billed at 1.2x the published rate and tracked in the month-to-date reconciliation.
  * Hard-burst (emergency): temporary capacity above +25% subject to availability and billed at 1.5x the published rate; we'd require a short lead/notification for sustained hard-bursts.

- Caps & throttles: we do not hard-throttle during ramp unless capacity is exhausted. Instead we apply burst pricing and, if sustained >150% of committed for 3 consecutive days, we propose a joint review and temporary rate adjustments.

- Discount milestones: we can attach milestone discounts tied to MAP checkpoints:
  * Milestone 1 (P0 validation, end of month 1): 5% usage credit for month 2 if baseline SLA & perf tests pass.
  * Milestone 2 (2-week production pilot, end of month 2): 10% committed discount once you convert pilot to a committed tier (>=1M tokens/month).
  * Milestone 3 (full rollout, by day 90): additional 5% volume discount at >=5M tokens/month commit.

I've included a short example invoice in the rate card tab "RampExample" showing a 3-month ramp with a soft-burst event in month 1. If you want, Priyom can draft a redline-friendly language block for your PO that spells out the burst mechanics and invoice treatment.

Next steps: attaching the MAP + rate card; if that aligns, Priyom and I will prepare the procurement-friendly clause.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales, East
Redwood Inference
From: GreenWave Procurement <procure@greenwavehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sedra Reyes <sreyes@greenwavehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-03T14:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on MAP + ramp pricing questions

Markus / team,

Thanks for the doc. A couple of procurement-specific clarifications before we route to legal: 

1) Define "committed" clearly — is this a peak-day commit, average daily commit, or monthly aggregate? We need a single number for invoicing and for any penalty/credit calculations.
2) For soft-burst billing at 1.2x, will overage be netted against next month's committed volume (i.e., do bursts count toward meeting the next milestone)?
3) We need a guaranteed initial cap for the first 60 days to avoid unexpected spend while clinical teams evaluate (we can agree to a higher commit after day 60). Can Redwood propose a conservative cap that still allows realistic testing?

Procurement is open to milestone discounts, but finance requires the example invoice and an estimate of expected spend in months 1–3 under a realistic pilot profile.

Regards,
GreenWave Procurement
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: GreenWave Procurement <procure@greenwavehealth.com>, Sedra Reyes <sreyes@greenwavehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-04T10:15:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up on MAP + ramp pricing questions

Hi Procurement team —

Thanks for the precision — here's a procurement-ready, line-item clarifying language and a conservative cap proposal. I'll attach the same text to the SOW draft after you confirm.

1) Definition of committed volume:
   - Committed = average daily tokens multiplied by 30 (monthly avg). For invoicing we use the prior invoice month as baseline; for the ramp period the committed monthly target will be the signed MAP "Month-1" target (example below).

2) Treatment of soft-bursts: 
   - Soft-burst usage (up to +25% of daily committed average) is billed at 1.2x published rate and DOES count toward the monthly invoice tally; it will also count toward achieving any milestone thresholds in that month.
   - Example: if committed = 1,000,000 tokens/month and you use 1,200,000 tokens in Month 1 (includes a short soft-burst), the month invoice will show usage=1.2M at blended rate (committed rate for first 1M, soft-burst rate for 200k). That 1.2M counts toward milestone attainment.

3) 60-day conservative cap proposal (for evaluation):
   - Proposed initial cap = 1.5x the signed Month-1 committed baseline for days 1–60. Any usage above that cap will require pre-approval and will default to hard-burst pricing (1.5x).
   - We will provide daily usage reports and a 24-hour alert for expected sustained bursts >120% of baseline.

4) Pricing calls & discounts (line items):
   - Published base rate: $0.0006 per token ($0.60 per 1k tokens).
   - Soft-burst rate: 1.2x base = $0.00072 per token.
   - Hard-burst rate: 1.5x base = $0.0009 per token.
   - Milestone discounts (applied to base rate for subsequent months per signed MAP): 5% / 10% / additional 5% as described by Markus.

If that works, we'll add a short clause to the SOW that reads: "During the 90-day MAP evaluation period, Redwood will apply the 60-day conservative cap and soft-burst protections as above. Soft-burst billed at 1.2x, counted toward milestones; hard-burst requires notice and is billed at 1.5x."

I'll also include the example invoice tab from the rate card into the SOW package. Let me know if Procurement wants the sample numbers adjusted to a different Month-1 baseline.

Thanks — Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sedra + procurement team —

Quick technical note to support Priyom's commercial proposal: based on the prompts and average conversation lengths you shared in the demo, we estimate token efficiency improvements during the first 30–45 days as you enable prefix caching and KV reuse. Practically this means your effective tokens-per-call should drop ~8–12% as we tune the cache. That helps limit surprise spend during soft-bursts.

Also attaching a lightly redlined SOW (SOW_GWH_draft.docx) with the procurement language Priyom suggested and a sample Month-1 baseline at 1.2M tokens/month. If you prefer a lower conservative cap, we can update the numbers before routing to legal.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
